title: Rashi Peripherals Ltd - 544119 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Rashi Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue up ~49% YoY, but ~30% of growth is price, H1 cash flow negative and D/E rose to 0.76x on inventory build; supply-side signals are mixed, not discipline.

summary.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 49% YoY to ₹6,185 crore, with PAT up 121% to ₹131 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported record Q2 and H1 FY27 profits on both standalone and consolidated bases, with H1 PAT more than doubling (transcript cites 54.5%) and H1 profit exceeding 80% of FY26's full-year profit. Growth was attributed to pricing (about 30% of growth, per management), non-PC mix, and the consolidation of VDA Info Solutions (67% stake), which contributed from Q2. Working capital days improved to 55 from 61, but net cash flow for the half was negative and debt-to-equity rose to 0.76x, which management tied to deliberate inventory build ahead of supply constraints and the Diwali timing shift. Management also discussed a possible QIP of up to ₹900 crore, framed as optional growth capital.

financial_highlights.metric: Q2 depreciation run-rate post VDA consolidation

segments.name: Core PC and IT distribution
segments.commentary: Management said the business is ~70% commercial demand and that non-PC products (accessories, CPUs) are 35-37% of the business, supporting margin. Pricing contributed about 30% of H1 growth.

segments.name: VDA Info Solutions (67% stake)
segments.commentary: Consolidated from Q2; management said VDA is under 2% of revenue so far, with only about one month in the quarter. Integrates system integration, cyber security, cloud and managed services.

segments.name: Semiconductor (Resta JV)
segments.commentary: Semiconductor revenue was about ₹20 crore last year; management targets 3-4x last year's numbers in the first six months of this year. Management said margins are roughly 2x company level.

segments.name: Enterprise and AI data centre
segments.commentary: Management said it chose not to pursue more than ₹20,000 crore of orders placed in one quarter, citing large exposure and low ROI. It targets enterprise at about 20% of business next year.

guidance_outlook: Sustainable EBITDA margin estimated at around 2.75% for FY29-FY30 once capex is used.
Management expects 10-15% price increases to contribute in H2, mainly in DRAM and flash.
H2 consumer demand expected to decline; commercial demand expected flat to positive.
Interest cost guided to remain in the same range as H1, including acquisition debt.
Debt-to-equity to be kept up to about 1:1, excluding temporary opportunities.
Indian ICT industry seen growing at least 10-12% in units; management said it does not need QIP capital and may not raise it at all.
capex_capacity: A possible ₹900 crore raise would add about ₹1,800-2,000 crore of deployable capital at 1:1 debt-to-equity, supporting about ₹12,000-15,000 crore of additional revenue at 6-7x working capital cycles.
Management said the QIP is an advance preparation for growth capacity, not a current need, and that it would be done in a calibrated manner.
Branch network: 57 branches, 50 service centres and 728 locations across India.
Inventory built to secure supply in a constrained market; management said VDA acquisition debt will be converted to cash in H2 and reported next quarter.
demand_pricing: India PC market grew about 12% in April-June quarter, led by commercial, education, small business and premium/AI-capable notebooks.
Price increases contributed about 30% of H1 growth; management expects 10-15% price rise in H2, with DRAM and flash the main drivers, though prices are flattening.
Management attributed inventory build to Diwali falling in late October this year versus 20 October last year, delaying a stock cycle into end-September and October.
Management said post-COVID, a 10-15% price correction did not hurt distribution because of expansion into new products, territories and customers.
Management said it is competing for AI data centre projects but has chosen not to pursue large low-ROI orders for now.

qa_highlights.question: Why was inventory built so strongly this quarter if consumer demand is softening, and what is the rationale for a QIP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the consumer impact was minuscule and commercial demand (about 70% of ICT) stayed strong; the build was due to the Diwali timing shift. QIP is advance preparation for capacity; management may not raise it at all and would stage it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin for FY29-FY30 and how much AI-related mix is expected over the next 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said around 2.75% EBITDA margin is a safe long-term assumption. No explicit AI mix guidance was given; management cited India's low AI penetration and a large opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: What drove margin resilience in Q2 (value vs volume)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited strong demand, pricing discipline (price contributing about 30% of growth), and non-PC mix at 35-37% of business. It said this is partly seasonal and not necessarily sustainable at this level.

qa_highlights.question: What does the Resta JV bring and is it exclusive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Resta is a Japanese semiconductor distributor; the JV brings new products, design capability, and access to Japanese OEMs in India. Exclusivity may be partial and the agreement is not yet formalised.

qa_highlights.question: Will prices correct and how should debt-to-equity be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 10-15% price rises in H2 and sees prices flattening. It targets debt-to-equity up to 1:1, with the current 0.76x including acquisition debt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for enterprise and semiconductor, and the H2 volume mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for enterprise at about 20% of business next year. For H2, it expects consumer to decline, while commercial demand could be flat to positive.

risks_watch: Negative cash flow and rising debt-to-equity (0.76x) from inventory build; management said inventory unwinds in H2 and VDA debt will convert to cash.
Price reversal risk if supply eases; management cited post-COVID price falls of 10-15% as a precedent.
Dilution concern: a ₹900 crore QIP was viewed by an analyst as about 15% of market cap; management suggested a calibrated approach.
Consumer demand softness in H2 and the impact of the Diwali timing shift on quarterly comparisons.
Resta JV exclusivity and formalisation still pending; semiconductor and VDA contributions are still small and need to be tracked.
Intangibles and goodwill from VDA consolidation; the new run-rate of ₹12 crore per quarter depreciation (incl. amortisation) and ₹7 crore ESOP amortisation to track.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, margins and growth, with a clear focus on profit quality. Cautious on balance sheet (negative cash flow, rising debt) and evasive on forward AI mix and QIP size, which management said may not happen.
key_quotes: So the expansion is coming from mix and pricing discipline not only operating leverage.
Both reflect deliberate choice we built inventory to secure supply in a constrained market.
We do not need this growth capital. We probably may not do a QIP at all.

growth.why: No numeric top-line guidance given; management expects 10-15% price rises in H2 (mainly DRAM/flash), consumer demand to degrow in H2 while commercial is flat to positive, and the industry to grow 10-12% in units, with H1 growth mostly from pricing and mix; the 2.75% sustainable EBITDA margin and enterprise at ~20% of business next year are the only other forward figures.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin rose 106 bps to 3.56% on pricing (about 30% of H1 growth) and non-PC mix at 35-37%, but management says Q2 strength is partly seasonal and the long-term sustainable EBITDA margin is only about 2.75%, so expansion beyond current levels is not assured.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management calls the possible ₹900 crore QIP advance preparation for growth capacity, not a current need, and says it may not raise it at all; no plant or line timing was given, and the branch network stands at 57 branches and 50 service centres.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Consumer demand is expected to decline in H2 while commercial demand (about 70% of business) is guided flat to positive, and the industry is seen growing 10-12% in units, so company volume growth is likely to be modest and mix-led.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said it does not need QIP capital and may not raise it at all, and it declined over ₹20,000 crore of large low-ROI enterprise and AI data-centre orders; no utilisation level was disclosed, so there is no capacity-driven push for a new capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects 10-15% price increases in H2 (DRAM and flash) and H1 consolidated PAT rose 95% to ₹225 crore, but it flagged that prices are flattening and Q2 strength is partly seasonal.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Price reversal risk if supply eases (management cited a 10-15% post-COVID price correction as precedent), H2 consumer demand is expected to decline, and inventory built ahead of Diwali must unwind.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Semiconductor revenue via the Resta JV is targeted at 3-4x last year's ~₹20 crore in H1, with margins about 2x company level, but the agreement is not yet formalised and exclusivity is partial.

rows.label: VDA acquisition debt converted to cash in H2
rows.why: Management said acquisition debt will be converted to cash in H2 and reported next quarter, with inventory unwinding; debt-to-equity is 0.76x against a target of about 1:1.

rows.label: Inventory unwind and working-capital release
rows.why: Working capital days improved to 55 from 61 and management said the inventory build (Diwali shift from 20 Oct to late Oct) unwinds in H2, which should reverse the negative H1 net cash flow.

rows.label: Enterprise share rising to about 20% of business
rows.why: Management targets enterprise at about 20% of business next year, but it declined large low-ROI AI data-centre orders, so the ramp is conditional.

tone.note: Management was confident on commercial demand, pricing and profit quality, and cautious on the balance sheet (negative cash flow, D/E 0.76x) and on QIP size and AI mix; analysts pressed on the ₹900 crore QIP dilution (about 15% of market cap) and on the sustainability of Q2 margins.
